items.title: "Buwaya Baby" Interdisciplinary Fashion Show
items.locationLabel: ARTS at King Street Station 303 South Jackson Street, Top Floor Seattle, WA 98104
items.venueAddress: ARTS at King Street Station 303 South Jackson Street, Top Floor Seattle, WA 98104
items.summary: Join ARTS at King Street Station for Buwaya Baby , an interdisciplinary fashion show and installation by Heidi Grace Acuña. HGA invites you to honor the start of Filipino American History Month with her fashion-based interdisciplinary show that brings their Buwaya Baby portal to life with a team of 20+ collaborators. HGA's artist residency at ARTS at King Street Station culminates in this interdisciplinary fashion show exploring Filipino folklore, spirituality, and heritage in the Philippines and in the US diaspora. We Still Dream a Future is a series of free public art activations, installations, exhibitions, performances, and learning experiences designed to help us dream, learn, and grow, taking place throughout the Downtown core. Gallery hours are Wed. – Sat. 11 a.m. – 5 p.m.; First Thursdays 11 a.m. – 8:00 p.m. Artist bio: Heidi Grace Acuña (@heidigraceacuna) Heidi Grace Acuña is an artist who creates to live. Born in Federal Way, Washington to immigrant Filipino parents, and raised on O‘ahu since one year old, Heidi felt disconnected to a true sense of home and belonging. Now, Heidi makes art that finds the beauty in the multiplicities of identity, culture, gender, and home. HGA’s interdisciplinary work in ceramic sculpture, fashion design, installation, and performance aims to create a legacy for our descendants where they may thrive beyond borders of identity, place, or possibility. IHA (@agimat.iha) IHA (they/them) is a storyteller, sound collager, and a dreamer. Born in Cavite and based in so-called "Vancouver", their work combines made and found sound into compositions that move between shades of playful and cataclysmic. They create immersive environments shaped by context and diasporic memory, with an intuitive approach to evolving rhythms and modulation. They are the founder of the imprint and collective Naga, whose releases and events blur genre conventions while fostering collaborative experimentation and collective play. Together with ephemeral objects, they perform as the audiovisual and DJ duo i+eo. Their debut work, Portals, premiered at MUTEK Montréal in 2025. Sade Aset (@sade_aset) Sade Aset (she/her) is a choreographer, director and free-time astrologer who graduated from Pacific Lutheran University with a BFA in Acting/Directing, and minors in French and Dance. Her work has been on the stages of Village Theatre, The 5th Avenue Theater, and many local high schools and community theaters. Additionally, she's worked as a producer, director, choreographer, editor, and music composer for screen dance/dance film. As an artist, she desires to create innovative and elaborate work, inspired by avant-garde, absurdist and psychologically invested themes and aesthetics. More of her work can be found at: sadeasetcd.com Michelle Mai Smith (@beautybymichellemai) Michelle Mai Smith is a makeup artist and hairstylist with over 12 years of experience working in the commercial, film and entertainment industries. She has been a proud member of IATSE Local 488 since 2021 and loves to share her passions related to arts, music and entertainment with a special commitment to sustainable and equitable practices.

items.title: Ferris Bueller's Day Off at Outdoors On The Ave
items.locationLabel: Square at U District Station 4301 Brooklyn Ave NE
items.venueAddress: Square at U District Station 4301 Brooklyn Ave NE
items.summary: One student, one stolen Ferrari, and one perfect skipped day in Chicago while an entire school system tries and fails to catch him. John Hughes made a movie about the specific joy of getting away with something, and it has never stopped feeling like permission. Closing the season with it is deliberate: life moves pretty fast, and this is the last outdoor movie of the year. You know what happens if you don't stop and look around. Ferris Bueller's Day Off (1986, PG-13) All movies are free and begin at dusk. Hosted by U District Advocates. Funding provided by 4Culture of King County and Amazon. Movies screened by our local Scarecrow Video.

items.title: Fishermen's Fall Festival
items.locationLabel: Fishermen's Terminal - Seattle 3919 18th Ave W, Seattle, WA 98119
items.venueAddress: Fishermen's Terminal - Seattle 3919 18th Ave W, Seattle, WA 98119
items.summary: Fishermen’s Fall Festival is a free event organized by a group of people and organizations to raise money for Seattle Fishermen’s Memorial; a non-profit organization dedicated to providing essential services to fishermen and their families while also honoring those lives lost at sea. An all-volunteer committee organizes this event that also educates the public about Fishermen’s Terminal and the North Pacific Fishing Fleet, and celebrates the commercial seafood industry at the heart of Seattle’s history. Attendees can expect a variety of fun and educational activities that bring to life the unique character of the historic Fishermen’s Terminal.

items.title: Grief Rituals: reflections on migration and mourning
items.locationLabel: ARTS at King Street Station 303 South Jackson Street, Top Floor Seattle, WA 98104
items.venueAddress: ARTS at King Street Station 303 South Jackson Street, Top Floor Seattle, WA 98104
items.summary: Join ARTS at King Street Station for Grief Rituals , a ritual performance by Little Brown Language. Grief Rituals is a multi-sited public performance and neighborhood procession exploring migration as a form of loss that shapes processes of cultural encounter and syncretism, ancestral memory and translation. Mixing dance, song, poetry and visual art, the Little Brown Language performance group will activate key locations moving from Seattle's Chinatown International District, to King Street Station and Waterfront Park. In doing the transformative work of collective grief, we reimagine connection with others, through which entangled forms of solidarity may emerge. SCHEDULE: Migration Procession Itinerary* 11:30 AM / Gathering and Petition at A Resting Place / 670 South King Street 12:10 PM / Departing A Resting Place 1:20-1:30 PM / Arriving King Street Station Plaza / 303 South Jackson Street 2-2:30 PM / Arriving ARTS at King Street Station Gallery / 303 South Jackson Street, Floor 3 3:30-3:45 PM / Departing ARTS at King Street Station Gallery 4-4:20 PM / Arriving Migration Stage / 199 Alaskan Way 5:30 PM / Communal Reflection Prayer on Habitat Beach 9 PM to midnight / Grief Rituals After Party / 12th Avenue Arts, 1620 12th Avenue *all times approximate and subject to change Register to stay informed. More information at: Grief Rituals Guidebook + Interactive Map We Still Dream a Future is a series of free public art activations, installations, exhibitions, performances, and learning experiences designed to help us dream, learn, and grow, taking place throughout the Downtown core. Gallery hours are Wed. – Sat. 11 a.m. – 5 p.m.; Thursdays 11 a.m. – 8:00 p.m. Artist bio: Little Brown Language (LBL) is a Seattle-based performance group who exist to build new forms of solidarity among local artist-organizers through embodied cultural practice. We are guided by a collective commitment to healing our relations with land and lineage. We create worlds in which the hidden histories of our communities become embodied, felt and seen.

items.title: Unite: A BIPOC Improv Jam
items.locationLabel: Langston Hughes Performing Arts Institute 104 17th Avenue South West Room Seattle, WA 98144
items.venueAddress: Langston Hughes Performing Arts Institute 104 17th Avenue South West Room Seattle, WA 98144
items.summary: Unite: A BIPOC Improv Jam is a monthly, free night of creativity and solidarity, and a welcoming space designed for BIPOC individuals of all skill levels to explore the art of improv. No experience is required, just an open mind! ​ Improv is about more than just comedy; it’s about connection. In this jam, we’ll use classic games and creative exercises to: ​ Support each other’s creative risks. ​Explore storytelling through music, movement, and poetry. ​ Celebrate our unique perspectives through spontaneous play. Unite: A BIPOC Improv Jam takes place every 1st Wednesday of the month (except for December’s jam) from 6:00 to 8:00 PM.

items.locationLabel: Garfield Community Center 2323 E Cherry St Seattle, WA 98122
items.venueAddress: Garfield Community Center 2323 E Cherry St Seattle, WA 98122
items.summary: In this workshop, you'll learn more about Arts in Parks and how to submit your best application. This program supports grassroots organizations, community-based groups, and individual artists seeking to activate Seattle parks through arts and culture in underserved and economically constrained areas of the city. This grant supports new and established festivals or events that promote arts and cultural participation, celebrate diversity, and build community connections while connecting with communities and audiences from historically unserved and/or underserved communities that represent Seattle’s diversity.
